title: Focal-SAM: Focal Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Long-Tailed Classification
publication_status_observed: ICML 2025 (Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, Vancouver, Canada, PMLR 267, 2025)
main_claims: Global SAM and ImbSAM provide either coarse or computationally expensive control over class-wise sharpness in long-tailed settings; Focal-SAM achieves fine-grained class-wise sharpness control without extra backpropagations.
Focal-SAM's generalization bound is sharper (O(1/n) rate) than SAM or CC-SAM (O(1/sqrt(n)) rate).
Focal-SAM consistently outperforms SAM-based baselines on long-tailed recognition and long-tailed OOD generalization tasks.
methodology: Focal-SAM assigns focal-mechanism weights (decreasing from head to tail classes) to class-wise sharpness terms, achieving fine-grained control without per-class backpropagation. The method is evaluated on CIFAR-10 LT, CIFAR-100 LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist using ResNet backbones from scratch, and also on CLIP fine-tuning. OOD evaluation uses ImageNet-Sketch, ImageNetV2, and ImageNet-C. Generalization is analyzed via PAC-Bayesian bounds.
key_results: Focal-SAM reduces training time to ~1.36x SAM on CIFAR-10 LT vs. CC-SAM's ~2.05x overhead.
Focal-SAM improves OOD performance by approximately 0.5%~4.3% when combined with baselines on ImageNet-C and other OOD test sets.
The PAC-Bayesian generalization bound for Focal-SAM decreases at O(1/n) rate vs. O(1/sqrt(n)) for SAM and CC-SAM.
Focal-SAM flattens loss landscape for both head and tail classes (lower lambda_max and Tr(H)), whereas ImbSAM sharpens head classes.
limitations: Focal-SAM requires class frequency information (pi_y) during training, limiting applicability to settings without class labels or known class distributions.
The hyperparameters gamma and lambda require tuning; the paper notes that the estimated perturbation radius could deviate from optimal without careful tuning.
OOD evaluation is limited to ImageNet-scale long-tailed settings; CIFAR-C style corruption benchmarks are not the primary focus.
relevance_to_rq: Peripheral relevance: Focal-SAM is a SAM variant for long-tailed learning, not the CIFAR-C corruption robustness setting of our study. It does evaluate on ImageNet-C (an OOD benchmark), providing some connection to the ood_benchmarks sub-topic, but the study's focus on class imbalance rather than representation stability under corruptions makes it tangential to the core RQ.

key_quotes.text: ImbSAM is efficient but offers only coarse control as it excludes head classes from the SAM process. On the other hand, CC-SAM provides fine-grained control through class-dependent perturbations but at the cost of efficiency due to multiple backpropagations.
key_quotes.context: Motivation: characterizing the efficiency-vs-control tradeoff problem in long-tail SAM variants that Focal-SAM addresses

key_quotes.text: Focal-SAM improves performance by approximately 0.5%∼4.3% when combined with baselines on OOD test sets.
key_quotes.context: Key OOD generalization result for Focal-SAM on long-tailed domain generalization tasks

key_quotes.text: The generalization bound consists of three components. Specifically, (III) decreases at a faster rate of O_tilde(1/n).
